subject: Request: Observability & Monitoring Exception for Private On-Prem Deployment
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena@stratoscope.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@stratoscope.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observability requirement for on-prem private deployment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Our security and SRE teams reviewed the proposed private deployment topology and requested an exception request: because Stratoscope will host the inference nodes inside our co-lo and manage the cross-connects, we need a carveout to allow Stratoscope-controlled observability endpoints (Prometheus scrape targets and application logs) to remain under our control.

Specifically, the asks are:
- Redwood will not mandate outbound monitoring agents that send full telemetry to redwood-managed endpoints; instead, Stratoscope will run local collectors and share aggregated metrics (percentiles and error rates) via a signed S3 artifact or push to an agreed HTTPS endpoint.
- Redwood agrees to a reduced SLA attribution window for latency spikes caused by customer-managed network (we propose a 15-minute attribution tail).
- Redwood will include a monitoring-visibility appendix in the SOW that documents what telemetry Redwood must receive for incident response vs. what can remain behind our firewall.

We'd like to capture this as an amendment to the Private Deployment Addendum. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept those terms (or propose counter-language)? I attached our network diagram for context.

Thanks,
Elena Gomez
Head of Infrastructure, Stratoscope

Attachment: stratoscope-network-diagram.png (png)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@stratoscope.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@stratoscope.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability requirement for on-prem private deployment

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clarity and the diagram. Short answer: we can get very close, but we need to align on a few specifics so incident detection and failover behave predictably. High-level proposed approach:

- Local collectors: OK. Stratoscope runs collectors; Redwood requires signed, timestamped metric bundles (or push to an authenticated HTTPS endpoint) at 5-minute intervals for key SLO metrics (token latency p50/p95, GPU throttling events, request error counts).
- Attribution window: we can accept an extended customer-network attribution tail, but suggest 30 minutes for initial agreement while we gather telemetry; after a three-month observation period we can reassess to 15 minutes if the telemetry indicates stable network behavior.
- Appendix: we'll draft monitoring-visibility language and show the exact metric names and thresholds.

I’m looping in Monica (Legal & Contracts) and Rishi (SRE) so we can draft amendment language and confirm feasibility from the runtime side.

Next steps:
1) Monica to propose amendment language (we will attach a redlined PDF).
2) Rishi to confirm the feasibility of accepting aggregated metric bundles and fallback behavior.
3) Elena/Procurement to confirm acceptance or counterproposals.

If it helps, Rishi and I can hop on a 30-min call with your SREs later this week.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@stratoscope.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@stratoscope.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T11:29:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability requirement for on-prem private deployment

Elena and team —

Thanks for the note. From contracts perspective we can add an "Observability & Attribution Appendix" to the Private Deployment Addendum that:
- Enumerates required metrics (as Soojin suggested) that Redwood must receive to perform SLA attribution and remedial actions.
- Allows for customer-hosted collectors and aggregated delivery, provided bundles are signed and timestamped.
- Defines the initial attribution tail at 30 minutes with an automatic review after 90 days.
- Calls out confidentiality and retention limits for telemetry artifacts.

I will produce a redline and attach as a PDF. A few legal asks:
- Please confirm the intended retention period for local logs and whether Stratoscope will redact PII before sharing artifacts.
- Confirm whether Stratoscope requires SLA credits for incidents attributed to customer network vs. Redwood (we should define credit calculation).

Attaching a draft amendment (internal redline) for review.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sla-amendment-observability-v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Elena Gomez <elena@stratoscope.com>
Date: 2028-03-16T07:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability requirement for on-prem private deployment

Elena — quick technical note from SRE:

We can accept aggregated metric bundles, but need the following to make incident response workable:
- Bundles must include epoch timestamps and request-id sampling at 1% (min) for error tracing; without any request-level trace we cannot root-cause complex P95+ errors.
- HTTPS push to our ingest endpoint must be mutually authenticated (mTLS) and we need a fallback S3 pull option if pushes fail for two consecutive intervals.
- For latency attribution, Redwood will initially apply the 30-minute network-tail. If the bundle shows customer-side packet loss >0.5% during the event window, the incident will be attributed to customer network. Otherwise standard attribution applies.

Also recommending an ops runbook in the appendix: contact matrix, escalation timeline, and a gated rollback policy for config changes that affect telemetry exports.

Happy to review your collector config or join a call to test a sample bundle.

— Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Gomez <elena@stratoscope.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@stratoscope.com>, ops@hypergrid.ai
Date: 2028-03-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability requirement for on-prem private deployment

Thanks all — this is helpful. A few clarifications from Stratoscope SRE:
- We can provide 1% sampled request IDs for error tracing (redacted PII), and we can implement mTLS to Redwood's ingest endpoint.
- Retention: we'll keep local logs for 60 days and share aggregated bundles for 90 days; PII will be redacted before transfer.
- For SLA credits: Stratoscope requests a binding formula for credit calculation that maps minutes of customer-network-attributed downtime to a pro-rated monthly service credit (we propose 1% credit per 30m outage, capped at 30%).

We approve the 30-day observation note for reassessment at 90 days. Please send the redline and a final amendment for signature (we would prefer DocuSign).

Elena

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena@stratoscope.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Procurement <procure@stratoscope.com>
Date: 2028-03-17T17:44:00-07:00
Subject: Observability Appendix — proposed amendment and next steps

Elena / team —

Attached is a redlined amendment that incorporates the telemetric bundle requirements, a 30-minute attribution tail with a 90-day review, the mTLS/S3 fallback mechanism, and confidentiality/retention clauses. I also added a simple credit formula aligned to your proposal (1% credit per 30m attributed outage, cap 30%).

If acceptable, please confirm and I will transmit the final DocuSign envelope. We will also include the ops runbook as an addendum for joint signoff.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Monica Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-sla-amendment-observability-v1.pdf, ops-runbook-draft.txt
